title: Shipping AI That Works: An Evaluation Framework for PMs – Aman Khan, Arize
talk_summary: Arize PM Aman Khan demos an eval workflow for a multi-agent trip planner: trace the agent, pull a span into a prompt playground, build a labeled dataset, run A/B prompt experiments, then LLM-as-judge evals validated against human labels. The core transferable ideas are label-not-score judging, judge-vs-human agreement checks, and eval-as-acceptance-criteria.

takeaways.technique: Label-based LLM judge instead of numeric scores
takeaways.what_they_do: Judges emit a text label (friendly/robotic, discount/no-discount) that is mapped to a score downstream, because LLMs are unreliable at producing numbers directly.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they're still really bad at numbers... give a text label that you can map to a score

takeaways.what_they_do: They hand-label a sample, then run a code/LLM eval that checks whether the judge's label matches the human label, and iterate the judge prompt until agreement rises.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You need evals for your evals. You cannot get away from... You can't just trust the system
takeaways.numbers: Their friendliness judge matched human labels almost never (near 0% agreement) on first pass

takeaways.what_they_do: Pull real spans from traces into a tabular dataset, run A/B prompt experiments over the whole set, and treat the eval+dataset as the PRD acceptance criteria.
takeaways.evidence_quote: instead of giving them a PRD, you give them an eval as requirements and here's the eval data set

takeaways.technique: Low temperature + rerun to control judge variance
takeaways.what_they_do: When judge labels are flaky, lower temperature and/or rerun the eval multiple times to profile variance.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you make the temperature of the model lower... it does significantly reduce the variance

takeaways.what_they_do: Instrument agents with OpenTelemetry spans (agent/tool/LLM) and render the call graph so you can see parallel branches and where outputs flow.
takeaways.evidence_quote: what does our agent actually look like... do you have a visualization to show me of like what the system actually looks like

takeaways.technique: Prompt playground with production variables + versioned prompt hub
takeaways.what_they_do: Pull a real trace's prompt template and variables into a playground, iterate, save versions, and A/B across a dataset before shipping.
takeaways.evidence_quote: being able to take your data and your prompts together and be able to iterate on your data and prompts in one interface
takeaways.numbers: Constraining output length cut latency from ~32s avg to much faster
